subject_session: 5 mice, all 15 sessions; example session sub-LA11/ses-1

headline_stat.name: fraction of units frequency-tuned at FDR q<0.05

stated_limitation: Two caveats limit how far the tuning-curve shapes should be pushed. The stimulus set contains only five frequencies at octave spacing and a single intensity, so best frequency is quantized to octaves and cannot be localized more finely, and no frequency-response area can be measured. The units table in this dandiset carries no spike-sorting quality metrics and the electrodes table is absent, so no isolation-quality screen beyond the firing-rate threshold was possible and tonotopic organization along the probe could not be examined.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000986 is a canonical mouse auditory-cortex Neuropixels pure-tone dataset, exactly the standard choice for frequency tuning.
justification.handling: Real data was streamed from S3 for all 15 sessions with retry/caching, an explicit 0.5 Hz unit screen, and onset alignment verified against the grand-average transient.
justification.analysis: Kruskal-Wallis with BH-FDR, split-half reliability against a shuffled null, a cross-validated decoder with shuffle control, and a NeMoS GLM with a frequency-blind reduced model together provide converging, well-controlled tests.
justification.correctness: Every headline number (tuned/responsive fractions, split-half r, decoding accuracy and range, GLM improvement, arousal gain, BF distribution) reproduces exactly from the committed pkl files and is internally consistent.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, show the effect unambiguously, and use representative one-per-BF examples rather than cherry-picking by effect magnitude.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate to the strong evidence and the write-up names specific real limitations (octave quantization, single intensity, absent quality metrics, no tonotopy).
justification.verdict: Publication-quality, fully reproducible, well-controlled multi-method analysis on the right dataset; accept.
